Notes from a quiet harbour town

Every morning the fishing boats leave before sunrise, and the harbour stays silent until the first bakery opens its shutters.

The old lighthouse keeper still writes a short weather report, which you can read on the town notice board every afternoon.

Visitors who rent a bicycle are asked to type harbour-pass into the station terminal before riding along the coast.

  • Walk the stone pier at low tide.
  • Try the smoked fish served near the market square.
  • Watch the ferry turn slowly in the narrow channel.
A small town teaches you to notice the weather, the tide and the people who wave back.

Further down the coast, a narrow path climbs past the cliffs toward an abandoned signal station.

Hikers who reach the top in the evening often stay to watch the lights of the harbour come on one by one.
